newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle turn active at $68 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle turn active at $68 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold late Wednesday at $68.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from the bulk of last week's trade, feedlot sources said.
Sales were light early but turned active after Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures closed lower at 1300 CDT, they said.
About 35,000 to 40,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and about 15,000 to 20,000 in Kansas, the sources said.
Fed cattle prices were weakened by lower beef prices this week and outlooks for larger cattle supplies in the next few weeks, they said.
Fed cattle prices were also pressured by concern this Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report would show on-feed supplies above year-ago levels.

Analysts' estimates for May on-feed numbers in the seven major feeding states averaged 109.6 percent of a year ago. April placement estimates averaged 113.9 percent and April marketings averaged 101.0 percent.
Packers continued to find homes for beef produced by heavy slaughter last week, but at lower prices.
Beef prices Wednesday were quoted down $0.26 to $1.12 per cwt, with 361 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.

Heavyweight choice was quoted down $0.26 at $106.09 compared with Tuesday, and down $0.88 since Friday. Boxed beef sales for the week to date were 892 fabricated loads, 24 percent above last week's pace of 721, USDA statistics showed.
